answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the vault embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the walnut index is rebuilt each epoch, the knoll audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 76% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 11 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
